result:
I'd make it painless for people to change their minds.

So much of what goes wrong in the world, from failed policies to feuds to institutions doubling down on mistakes, persists not because no one knows better, but because admitting error costs too much. People lose status, their side loses ground, and their past selves look foolish. So they defend positions long after they've privately stopped believing them, and problems that could be fixed stay broken.

If being wrong felt like a normal, even slightly pleasant, part of learning, I think a lot of other problems would get easier. Science would move faster, politics would be less tribal, and relationships would recover from conflicts more easily. It wouldn't solve everything, but it would improve our ability to solve everything else.

The obvious competitor is something more direct, like ending extreme poverty or disease, and I can see the argument that concrete suffering should come first. But I'm betting that a humanity better at updating would get to those faster anyway.

What would yours be?
